newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 - The slowdown in seasonal palm production in Sept exceeded earlier expectations. Our preliminary estimates show production rose four percent or some 30,000 tonnes, to 843,000 tonnes, as against our previous estimate of a six percent rise to 860,000 tonnes. As in August, the bulk of the increase was accounted by East Malaysia. In Peninsular Malaysia, production was practically flat during the month, with indications the peak has tapered off. The absence of a pronounced seasonal peak also suggests production will not drop sharply in the last three months of this year.

With production in Jan-Sept estimated at 6.07 million tonnes, there is a likelihood total production for the year will hit 6.3 million tonnes or slightly more than our June 26 projection of 8.26 million tonnes. For the second consecutive month, crude palm oil (CPO) production had comfortably exceeded offtake which rose an estimated 15,000 tonnes to around 755,000 tonnes. Consequently, there was a further buildup in CPO stocks to an estimated 560,000 tonnes at end Sept as against 472,000 tonnes a month earlier. With PO demand also tapering off, end Sept stocks of processed palm oil are estimated to have risen some 15,000 tonnes to 345,000 tonnes.

Total palm oil stocks thus amounted to an estimated 905,000 tonnes, an increase of around 105,000 tonnes over end August and substantially more than the year ago level of 574,000 tonnes and the end Sept level of 500,400 tonnes. After reaching an all-time high of 662,000 tonnes in July, palm oil exports in Sept were estimated at 645,000 tonnes or little changed compared to the preliminary Aug figure of 638,600 tonnes reported by PORLA. Indonesia's offtake of 22,000 tonnes plus an increase of 15,000 tonnes (to around 95,000 tonnes) by China could not offset the 70,000 tonnes reduction in shipments to Pakistan.

CPO futures recovered 18-30 ringgit in the week ended Sept 27 after having fallen 114 ringgit in the preceding two weeks. The modest recovery was attributed to active shortcovering activities in both cash and futures. Turnover in CPO futures on Sept 24 when prices jumped down 40-36 ringgit reached 4,756 lots (119,125 tonnes). The highest registered so far this year, however, continued slack in new export sales coupled with somewhat lower than expected Sept bulk shipment figures reported by surveyors saw CPO futures resuming its downtrend when prices retreated around 30 ringgit on Sept 30-Oct 1.

The announcement by Indonesia's state-owned marketing agency to temporarily suspend new export sales of CPO gave the market a knee-jerk reaction when prices recovered some 30 ringgit on another round of shortcovering activities. With U.S. soya market registering extended losses in the last two weeks in CBSBO trading at a discount to CPO late last week for up to December shipment, it would be tough for palm oil to hold on to the current price levels in the next few weeks. December CPO futures on Oct 7 settled at 1,145 ringgit or 11 ringgit dowm on Friday while N/D RBD olein was quoted at $530.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
